capabilities: Opens .toml and .ini files from the file explorer
Renders a parsed config tree with sections, keys, values, and type labels
Filters the tree and switches to a line-numbered source view
Reports TOML parse errors and INI duplicate-key, duplicate-section, and malformed-line warnings
Caps rendered nodes and refreshes after external file changes
extras: TOML is parsed with the smol-toml dependency; INI uses a local conservative parser. The parsed tree caps at 2,000 nodes, but the source view always shows the full file.
motivation: TOML and INI files rely on comments, ordering, whitespace, and tool-specific conventions that an editor can silently change, so the viewer never writes to disk.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to inspect TOML or INI config files, and editing them in a form editor or formatter could strip comments, reorder sections, or normalize syntax.
summary: Read-only viewer that opens .toml and .ini files as a searchable config tree with source view, parse warnings, and large-file caps.
